outline.target_audience: Advanced High School (AP Calculus) or First-year University Students

sections.title: The Mystery of the Tangled Equation
sections.content: Introduce the difference between 'Explicit' functions (y isolated) and 'Implicit' equations (x and y are mixed). Use a visual of a simple line versus a complex circle. Explain that while we can't always solve for y, we still need to find the slope (rate of change) at any point on the curve.
sections.example: Visualizing a 'Mathematical Rollercoaster' loop defined by x² + y² = 25. Note that isolating y creates two messy square-root functions, which we want to avoid.

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Chain Rule Secret
sections.content: Briefly review the Chain Rule, as it is the engine of implicit differentiation. Emphasize that when we see 'y', we must treat it as an 'invisible function of x' [y(x)]. Show the animation of d/dx acting on a function of y.
sections.example: If y is a 'mystery box' containing x, then d/dx [y³] isn't just 3y², it's 3y² · (dy/dx). Think of (dy/dx) as the 'inner derivative' footprint.

sections.title: Step 1: The 'Differentiate Both Sides' Blitz
sections.content: Demonstrate applying d/dx to every term on both sides of the equation simultaneously. Use color-coding: Blue for terms with only x, Red for terms with y (which require the Chain Rule).
sections.example: For x² + y² = 25: Applying d/dx gives [d/dx(x²)] + [d/dx(y²)] = [d/dx(25)]. This results in 2x + 2y(dy/dx) = 0.

sections.title: Step 2: Isolating the Target (dy/dx)
sections.content: Transition to algebraic manipulation. The goal is to get all terms containing (dy/dx) on one side and everything else on the other. Use an animation of terms 'jumping' across the equal sign and signs changing.
sections.example: From 2x + 2y(dy/dx) = 0, subtract 2x to get 2y(dy/dx) = -2x. Then divide by 2y to reveal the slope formula: dy/dx = -x/y.

sections.title: Visual Validation: The Radar Cat
sections.content: Apply the found derivative to a coordinate. Use a character 'Radar Cat' sitting at a specific point on the circle to calculate the local slope. Graphically show the tangent line appearing to prove the math matches the visual steepness.
sections.example: At point (3, 4) on our rollercoaster: dy/dx = -3/4. Radar Cat sees a downward slope. At point (0, 5), dy/dx = 0/5 = 0, showing a perfectly flat peak.

sections.title: Summary & Mastery Recap
sections.content: Summarize the 3-step workflow: 1. Differentiate everything (watch for y!), 2. Collect dy/dx terms, 3. Solve. Reinforce that implicit differentiation works even when the geometry is 'tangled'.
sections.example: A final graphic overlay showing a complex 'Lissajous curve' (a figure-8 shape) being solved using the same three steps.

storyboard.title: The Mystery of the Tangled Equation
lecture_lines: Explicit functions keep y isolated on one side.
Implicit equations mix x and y together.
Take this circle: solving for y creates messy roots.
Yet, every point on this curve has a slope.
Implicit differentiation reveals slope without isolating y.
animations: Create expressions 'y = 2x + 1' (Blue: #58C4DD) and 'x^2 + y^2 = 25' (Yellow: #FFFF00) at top.
Animate a pulsing white circle around 'y' in 'y = 2x + 1' to show isolation.
Draw a large yellow circle (#FFFF00) centered on the screen for 'x^2 + y^2 = 25'.
Show the text 'y = \pm \sqrt{25 - x^2}' appearing then covered by a red 'X' (#FF0000).
Display a large white question mark '?' at the center of the circle curve.

storyboard.title: Prerequisite: The Chain Rule Secret
lecture_lines: Treat y as an invisible function of x.
Derivative of y-cubed isn't just three y-squared.
We must multiply by the inner derivative, dy dx.
animations: Display the chain rule formula: d/dx [f(x)^3] = 3f(x)^2 \cdot f'(x).
Transform the formula into d/dx [y^3] = 3y^2 \cdot (dy/dx) by replacing f(x) with y.
Highlight (dy/dx) in bright red (#FF0000) and label it 'Inner Derivative Footprint'.

storyboard.title: Step 1: The 'Differentiate Both Sides' Blitz
lecture_lines: Apply the derivative operator to every single term.
Power rule handles x-squared normally, giving two x.
For y-squared, the chain rule adds dy dx.
The derivative of a constant, twenty-five, is zero.
Our equation now links x, y, and slope.
animations: Display the full equation x^2 + y^2 = 25 in the center.
Animate 'd/dx' operators appearing in front of each term on both sides.
Transform 'd/dx(x^2)' into '2x' using blue color (#58C4DD).
Transform 'd/dx(y^2)' into '2y \cdot (dy/dx)', with 'dy/dx' in red (#FF0000).
Simplify the equation view to 2x + 2y(dy/dx) = 0.

storyboard.title: Step 2: Isolating the Target (dy/dx)
lecture_lines: We need to isolate the target: dy dx.
First, subtract two x from both sides.
Now, divide both sides by two y.
Twos cancel, leaving negative x over y.
This formula calculates slope at any point.
animations: Start with the equation 2x + 2y(dy/dx) = 0.
Animate '2x' moving to the right side and changing to '-2x'.
Move '2y' to the denominator and box the final 'dy/dx = -x/y' in green (#83C167).

storyboard.title: Visual Validation: The Radar Cat
lecture_lines: At point three four, the slope is negative three-fourths.
At the peak zero five, the slope is zero.
Tangent lines perfectly match our calculated values.
animations: Draw the yellow circle and highlight point (3, 4) with a small dot.
Show calculation text: 'dy/dx = -3/4' appearing near the point.
Draw a tangent line through (3, 4) with slope -0.75.
Highlight point (0, 5) and show calculation 'dy/dx = -0/5 = 0'.
Draw a horizontal tangent line at the top of the circle (0, 5).

storyboard.title: Summary & Mastery Recap
lecture_lines: First, differentiate every term, using the chain rule.
Next, use algebra to solve for dy dx.
Now you can find slopes for any tangled curve.
animations: Show a numbered list: 1. Differentiate, 2. Isolate dy/dx, 3. Solve for slope.
Display a complex figure-8 (Lissajous) curve with several tangent arrows.
Show concluding text 'Implicit Differentiation: Unlocking Hidden Curves' in gold (#FFD700).
